ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Adrianople, the Visigothic sack of 410 and the loss of North Africa stripped the Western Empire of armies, prestige and revenue.
Alaric's Visigoths shattered the myth of Roman invulnerability, though the Western Empire limped on for another sixty-six years.
Once the commercial hub of the known world, the caliphate had long ceased to be a first-rank military power when the Mongols arrived.
The Mongol destruction of Baghdad in 1258 ended the caliphate there, although a shadow caliphate survived under the Mamluks in Cairo.
A civilisation that saw its own decline clearly: the loss of Anatolia and the crusader sack of 1204 did damage it never repaired.
On 29 May 1453 Mehmed II's cannon breached the Theodosian walls, extinguishing the Byzantine Empire after eleven centuries.
Fiscal strain, rebellions such as the Taiping and defeat in the Opium Wars hollowed out China's last dynasty from within and without.
An uprising at Wuchang in 1911 spread from province to province and led to Puyi's abdication, ending two thousand years of imperial rule.
The conqueror of Constantinople endured until defeat in the First World War and the abolition of the sultanate in 1922.
